newsitem.title: USA: AGA sees record U.S. natural gas demand in 1997.
newsitem.headline: AGA sees record U.S. natural gas demand in 1997.

text.p: The American Gas Association (AGA) said Wednesday that U.S. demand for natural gas this year should rise to its highest level ever, eclipsing a record set in 1972.

"Assuming normal weather, a growth of 2.5 percent in the U.S. economy and crude oil prices averaging $20.50 a barrel, AGA projects that natural gas use in 1997 will reach 23.2 quads (quadrillion British thermal units)," AGA president Michael Baly told a meeting of the New York Society of Security Analysts here.

Baly, who noted estimated 1996 usage of 22.8 quads also could surpass the 1972 record of 22.7 quads, said the projected 1.9 percent gain in demand this year would put consumption at the highest level ever achieved in the U.S.
The increase will continue a 10-year trend that has seen gas consumption rise by 36 percent since 1986.

"The residential market is really our foundatation. Space heating really drives gas demand and that's what happened last year," Baly said, adding he expected residential growth to decline slightly this year to 5.22 quads from 5.44 in 1996 with the return of more normal weather.

He said while space heating demand in the commercial market also should decline in 1997, gains in areas such as food services and space cooling should lead to a modest overall increase for the sector of about one percent to 3.44 quads.

Industrial usage, the largest gas consuming sector in the country, was projected to rise by 3.5 percent next year to 9.3 quads. Electric utility usage was expected to rise by 7.7 percent to 3.15 quads.
"This growing demand for natural gas can only be sustained if the supply is there to meet demand, and once again, our supply picture is excellent," Baly said.
He said 1996 U.S. gas well completions will exceed 1995 by approximately 15 percent and for the fourth straight year, gas well completions were expected to exceed oil well completions.
AGA estimates there were about 8,500 gas well completions in 1996 versus about 7,400 oil well completions.
Baly said Canadian exports to the U.S., which were relatively flat last year at 2.8 tcf (trillion cubic feet), have also helped meet demand.
On the price side, Baly said he expects a 1996 average wellhead price of about $2.26, up from 1995's $1.59.
